pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with CHECK; test 'AC-1' checks existing rows are normal and 'urgent' is rejected.
test 'AC-2' asserts labelled high/low and unlabelled normal output.
test 'AC-3' checks each filter lists only that priority in id order.
test 'AC-4' checks the unfiltered list in id order.
test 'AC-5' checks the exact nav for all four views, with the current one in <strong>.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__.

The code does this and the test body checks it, but the last commit (a40fc6e, 'Follow-up edits') renamed the test from 'AC-7: ...' to 'an unmatched filter...'. No test names AC-7 now, and the spec doesn't mark it 'verified by review'.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'; test 'AC-8' asserts it; the checker script accepts the query.

findings.what: Commit a40fc6e ('Follow-up edits', a bot commit) removed the 'AC-7:' prefix from the test title. No test names AC-7 now. By the rule that each item is named by its proving test, AC-7 is unmet. The PR claims the tests cover AC-1 to AC-8.
findings.fix: Restore 'AC-7' in the test title, ideally with a dedicated AC-7 test, and drop the unexplained follow-up commit.

findings.what: The README documents only the filter values. It doesn't mention the '— high'/'— low' labels, the 400 for invalid values, or the priority column.
findings.fix: Add one line on the labels and the 400 response.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec's intent. Nothing was added beyond the ask except the checker change the spec needs for AC-8.
AC-7 is no longer named by any test because of the last commit. The state-table rows each have a test.

The tests assert behaviour and would fail if the code were wrong. The traffic fake-app and checker tests were extended, not loosened. I did not run the suite (it needs Workers runtime dependencies; CI covers it).
The README is minimally updated and omits the labels and the 400 (low finding).
The query is parameterised, the priority is validated against an allowlist, and titles are escaped. I found no defects.
The SQL is bound, the input is allowlisted, and output is HTML-escaped. I found no planted instructions.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no UI framework or style files; the spec defines no visual design.
No browser flow was available. The rendered output is checked by the tests.
The claim that the tests cover AC-1 to AC-8 is not true of the final commit, because AC-7 lost its name. 'Changed after the go: nothing' is accurate for the spec.
